behavioral_contracts.description: Create collection then query it - collection should be visible immediately
behavioral_contracts.scenario: Create a collection via PUT /collections/{name}, then get it via GET /collections/{name}. The collection should be fully initialized and visible immediately after 200 response.
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: After a successful 200 response from create collection, a subsequent GET collection info request returns 200 with the collection configuration.

behavioral_contracts.description: Delete collection then query it - collection should not exist
behavioral_contracts.scenario: Delete a collection via DELETE /collections/{name}, then attempt to get it via GET /collections/{name}. The collection should no longer exist.
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: After a successful 200 response from delete collection, a subsequent GET collection info request returns 404.

behavioral_contracts.description: Upsert points and count - count should reflect the exact number of upserted points
behavioral_contracts.scenario: Upsert N points via PUT /collections/{name}/points, then count points via POST /collections/{name}/points/count with exact=true. The count should equal N.
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: After upserting N points successfully, exact count returns N.

behavioral_contracts.description: Upsert points and search - search should find the upserted points
behavioral_contracts.scenario: Upsert a point with a known vector, then search for that vector. The upserted point should appear in the search results.
behavioral_contracts.expected_behavior: After upserting a point, a search with the same vector returns the point among results (subject to eventual consistency if not waited).

state_invariants.description: After successful creation, collection should be queryable immediately
state_invariants.assertion: PUT /collections/{name} with 200 response guarantees subsequent GET /collections/{name} returns the collection info.

state_invariants.description: After successful deletion, collection should not exist
state_invariants.assertion: DELETE /collections/{name} with 200 response guarantees subsequent GET /collections/{name} returns 404.

state_invariants.description: Upserting N points then counting with exact=true returns N
state_invariants.assertion: After PUT /collections/{name}/points with N points (200 response), POST /collections/{name}/points/count with exact=true returns count=N.

state_invariants.description: Deleting points reduces the count accordingly
state_invariants.assertion: Deleting M points from a collection with N points results in the count being N-M (or less if fewer matched).

state_invariants.description: Multiple alias operations in one request are atomic
state_invariants.assertion: POST /collections/aliases with multiple actions applies all or none atomically.
